candidate.answerReason: The number of ounce charges is the least integer at least W, which equals -floor(-W), including at whole-ounce weights.

methods.label: Round up to the next whole ounce
methods.explanation:
Any fractional ounce requires a full six-cent charge, but an exact whole-ounce weight requires no extra charge. Thus, for a positive letter weight \(W\), let \(n\) be the positive integer satisfying
\[
n-1<W\le n.
\]
The letter requires \(n\) ounce charges, so its postage is \(6n\) cents. Negating the inequalities gives
\[
-n\le -W<-n+1.
\]
By the definition of the floor function, \(\lfloor-W\rfloor=-n\). Therefore the postage is
\[
6n=-6\lfloor-W\rfloor.
\]
The included endpoint \(W=n\) correctly gives exactly \(6n\) cents. The answer is \(\boxed{-6\lfloor-W\rfloor}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
